samples.summary: `saveSnapshot()` before `withUndoUnit()` costs a dead Cmd+Z on every MemDocStore-backed host (slides text boxes, docs demo, hunt/visual harness)
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit` documents (text-editor.ts:3807) that `saveSnapshot()` must run *before* the unit opens. On `YorkieDocStore` `snapshot()` is a no-op, so that is free — but `MemDocStore.snapshot()` pushes an undo checkpoint (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:181-183) and `MemDocStore.batch()` then pushes a *second, identical* checkpoint up front (memory.ts:206-209), keeping it because the body wrote (memory.ts:230-236). The repo already documents exactly this hazard and takes the opposite ordering for it: packages/docs/src/view/link-run.ts:81-85 — "`MemDocStore.batch()` takes its own checkpoint up front, so a call before the batch costs a second, identical undo step (a dead Cmd+Z) and clears the redo stack that `batch()` puts back" — and `withNamedStyleChange` puts `docStore.snapshot()` *inside* the batch (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1238-1239). Affected out-of-diff consumers: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:431/680/682 (Slides text boxes and Slides table cells run `TextEditor` over a `MemDocStore` with `saveSnapshot = docStore.snapshot()` and `undo = docStore.undo()`), packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1042 (default store when no store is passed: demo.ts, harness scenarios, revision-preview). Because `handleInput` wraps unconditionally (text-editor.ts:995-1001), *every* keystroke — not just selection-replacing ones — now leaves two identical undo entries there, so undo needs two presses per edit and the first-of-two looks like it did nothing. Existing docs tests only ever press undo once (e.g. packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts:790), so nothing catches it. Fix belongs on the new code: either call `saveSnapshot()` inside the unit (as link-run/withNamedStyleChange do) or have `withUndoUnit` take the snapshot itself.

samples.summary: Identity-based undo floor fails *open*: any SDK behaviour that recreates undo-stack entries re-opens the "undo destroys the initial block" crash
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` now returns `true` whenever `lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark)` misses (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2972-2977). The old depth comparison failed closed. The floor exists to stop undo unwinding `ensureTree`/`setDocument`, which leaves the caret pointing at a deleted block and crashes `handleInput` with "Block not found" — the regression pinned by packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:644-651. So the new logic is only safe if a stack entry object is *never* replaced while the initial-load prefix is still on the stack. I could not verify that: `@yorkie-js/sdk@0.7.19` is not installed in this checkout (no node_modules), so I could not read `pushUndo`/`history` to see whether entries are rebuilt on remote-change transformation, snapshot application, or detach/re-attach. If they are, the floor silently disappears and every initial-load entry becomes undoable. To confirm/refute: read the SDK's `Document.getUndoStackForTest`, `pushUndo`, and any remote-change/snapshot handling of `internalHistory` and check whether entries are ever re-created rather than mutated in place. A defensive form (`indexOf(mark) === -1 → refuse`, or re-arming the mark) would fail closed instead.

samples.summary: Three sibling Yorkie stores keep the depth-based undo floor the diff just declared broken, and their comments/design docs point at the now-removed `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`
samples.evidence: The same `getUndoStackForTest().length > undoFloor` comparison that this diff replaces (because the 50-entry cap makes a recorded depth stop describing the boundary) still lives at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:347/358/654/670, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:127/136/353, and packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:244/270/514 — so those surfaces still stop undo early once the cap evicts. Their doc-comments and the design docs also cite a symbol that no longer exists: yorkie-note-store.ts:125 ("Mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`"), yorkie-slides-store.ts:345, packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:49, docs/design/notes/notes.md:399, docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:183-209 and :323.

samples.summary: The render-hold wrapper only covers `requestRender`; the two render variants bypass it and the replay always uses the scrolling variant
samples.evidence: `requestRenderNoCursorScroll` (text-editor.ts:2249) and `requestCaretRender` (text-editor.ts:2961-2962, called from 3340/3359/3372/3387/3403) invoke the host callback directly, so if any of those sites ever runs inside a `withUndoUnit` body it paints mid-batch, and the deferred replay in `withUndoUnit`'s `finally` (3819-3822) fires the full scroll-to-caret `requestRender` regardless of which variant the interior asked for. No current unit body reaches them, so this is latent — but the deferral seam is now the invariant every future batched path depends on, and it is only wired for one of three render entry points.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out. text-editor.ts:995 calls saveSnapshot() outside the unit opened at :1001, and the body always writes (:1011). MemDocStore.snapshot() only short-circuits inside a batch (memory.ts:177-184), so at depth 0 it pushes a checkpoint and clears redo; MemDocStore.batch() then pushes a second, identical checkpoint up front (memory.ts:206-209) and keeps it because the body wrote (memory.ts:230-236). undo() (memory.ts:157-161) does not dedup identical states, so each keystroke leaves two identical undo entries and every second Cmd+Z/redo press is dead. Doc.batch() delegates directly to store.batch (document.ts:146-153). The repo itself documents this exact hazard and takes the opposite ordering: link-run.ts:81-85 with snapshot inside the batch at :101-102, and withNamedStyleChange at editor.ts:1238-1239. Out-of-diff consumers are real: text-box-editor.ts:431/680/682 (Slides text boxes and table cells over a MemDocStore) and editor.ts:1042 default store wired to docStore.snapshot() at editor.ts:2475. No guard makes it unreachable; this is a behaviour regression at sites the diff does not show, which is squarely in the blast-radius lane at major severity.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists as quoted (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2970-2978 identity-based floor; markUndoFloor at :858-861), but the finding is not a blast-radius defect. (a) No bypassing or broken call site exists in this repo: the only path to `doc.history.undo()` in the docs surface is `YorkieDocStore.undo()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2956-2958), which is gated by `canUndo()` on the line above, reached from `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:407` via `editor.undo()`; a repo-wide grep for `history.undo()` shows the other stores (yorkie-store.ts:1186, yorkie-note-store.ts:281, yorkie-slides-store.ts:637, yorkie-board-store.ts:501) each keep their own independent depth floor (yorkie-note-store.ts:136/353, yorkie-slides-store.ts:358/654, yorkie-board-store.ts:270/514) and are untouched by this change. (b) The asserted bypass is not a call site but a hypothesised internal behaviour of the un-installed third-party @yorkie-js SDK (no node_modules/@yorkie-js/** present) — that is the changed code depending on an upstream assumption, the reverse of this lens's direction (what this change breaks in code that depends on it). (c) The reviewer's evidence points at the diff lines themselves (2972-2977), which the rubric explicitly excludes ("evidence with the bypassing or broken site, not the diff line that introduced the guard"); restated plainly it is "this new condition fails open", a wrong-condition judgement statable without leaving the diff, which the rubric assigns to the correctness lens. Real-or-not is unresolved by design (SDK unreadable), but it is out of scope for blast radius either way.
